exact_interval.method: Clopper-Pearson: the lower bound L solves P(X >= x | n, L) = (1 - level)/2 and the upper bound U solves P(X <= x | n, U) = (1 - level)/2, by bisection on exact binomial sums; width = upper - lower from the rounded bounds

revisions_among_six.kind: computed: exact binomial probabilities for assumed true rates (scenarios.json, forecasters)

rate_15_percent.description: Revised 15% of the time: the most a forecaster calibrated at confidence 0.85 would be wrong.

rate_10_percent.description: Revised 10% of the time: calibrated at confidence 0.90.

rate_5_percent.description: Revised 5% of the time: calibrated at confidence 0.95.

rate_one_third.description: Revised one time in three: the recorded share, taken as the true rate. Overconfident under the lesson's reading.

calibrated_at_each_stated_confidence.note: Each of the six files is wrong with probability 1 - its own stated confidence, independently; 'revised' is read as 'wrong'. An assumption about the forecaster, applied to the observed confidences.

revisions_among_six.likelihood_ratio_definition: P(exactly the observed count | rate 1/3) / P(exactly the observed count | other rate)

flat_prior.prior: uniform on the true rate between 0 and 1
flat_prior.method: posterior Beta(x + 1, n - x + 1); P(rate > r) = P(Binomial(n + 1, r) <= x), checked against the integral of r^x (1 - r)^(n - x)

telling_two_rates_apart.kind: computed: exact binomial error rates of a counting rule; the error rates wanted are choices (scenarios.json, test)
telling_two_rates_apart.definition: Rule 'call the forecaster overconfident when c or more of n high-confidence beliefs are revised'. False alarm = probability of that at the calibrated rate; detection = probability at the other rate.

at_the_recorded_pace.assumption: High-confidence belief files keep being recorded at the pace of the six counted at the pin: six between the earliest last_updated among them and the timestamp of the record. This only sets a scale. The six were not recorded at a steady pace, and two of them are written by the applying script from recommendations.

nudge_rule.kind: observed rule (pinned files), applied by computation

upward_branch.note: The pinned pipeline specification has an upward branch driven by an underconfidence rate; the calibration belief records no such rate, so this fixture models the downward branch only.

nudge_over_cycles.kind: synthetic: exact probabilities and a seeded simulation under the assumption below; not a measurement of the project
nudge_over_cycles.assumption: Each cycle sees a fresh, independent sample of sample_per_cycle high-confidence beliefs from a forecaster whose true revision rate is fixed. The recorded loop does not work that way (it re-reads the same belief files on every cycle): this is the rule's best case, not a model of the project.
nudge_over_cycles.report_note: The policy schedules the calibrator weekly and human oversight at least quarterly: 13 cycles is one quarter of weekly cycles, 52 is one year.

rules.total_clamped_as_in_the_applier: Pinned rule: a recommendation is produced when the observed rate exceeds the trigger; its nudge is max(-cap, -gain * rate); the stored total is the previous total plus the nudge, clamped to [-cap, +cap].
rules.per_cycle_cap_only: The same nudge, capped per cycle as the policy's guardrail is worded, with no limit on the running total. Not what the pinned script does.
rules.two_sided_comparison_rule: Hypothetical, not in the repository: nudge = clamp(-gain * (observed rate - target), -cap, +cap), with the pinned gain and cap and the pinned trigger as target. It moves up when the observed rate is below the target and down when it is above. No limit on the running total.
rules.two_sided_with_the_total_clamp: The hypothetical two-sided rule with the stored total clamped to [-cap, +cap].

simulation.percentile_rule: nearest rank: the value at position ceil(q * runs / 100) of the sorted totals

stated_confidence.kind: observed value, set against a cited formula (scenarios.json, cited_producer)

cited_formula.formula: min(cap, base + per_belief_file * number of belief files read)

planted_move.note: In a copy of the snapshot, one current high-confidence belief is treated as archived. The recount and the rebuilt claim must both change.

provenance: the files whose only evidence is a recommendation are the two the applying script writes
the cap is the same in the pipeline formula, the applier, the policy guardrail and the belief file
binomial probabilities of all counts sum to 1
exact interval: the bracket of the lower bound holds the tail probability
exact interval: the bracket of the upper bound holds the tail probability
known answer: the exact 95% interval for 1 of 1 starts at 0.025 and the one for 0 of 1 ends at 0.975
larger samples keep the observed share exactly
exact interval: it narrows as the sample grows at a fixed share
probabilities: none + exactly one + two or more = 1
hand-computed case: P(2 or more of 6 at 15%) = 1 - 0.85^6 - 6 * 0.15 * 0.85^5
unequal probabilities: the count distribution sums to 1 and reduces to the binomial when all are equal
flat prior: the binomial identity equals the integral of the likelihood
decision rule: at every critical count the higher rate triggers the rule more often
decision rule: the critical count is the smallest one within the false-alarm limit
sample size: the sample before the smallest one fails the design
recorded cycle: the pinned formula and clamp reproduce threshold_nudge and applied_delta from prior_nudge
nudge chain: the probabilities of all totals sum to 1
nudge chain: closed form for the clamped total (still 0: q0^k; one small nudge: k q1 q0^(k-1))
known answer: simulated shares are within the stated tolerance of the exact probabilities
known answer: simulated mean totals are within the stated tolerance of the exact means
stated confidence: the cited formula gives the confidence the record states
negative control: a line no file reaches leaves zero high-confidence files
negative control: a line of 0 counts every belief file read
negative control: the planted file is a current belief
negative control: one belief treated as archived changes the recount and the rebuilt claim
